definition: Sentence extraction is a technique used for automatic summarization of a text.
details: In this shallow approach, statistical heuristics are used to identify the most salient sentences of a text. Sentence extraction is a low-cost approach compared to more knowledge-intensive deeper approaches which require additional knowledge bases such as ontologies or linguistic knowledge. In short, sentence extraction works as a filter that allows only meaningful sentences to pass. The major downside of applying sentence-extraction techniques to the task of summarization is the loss of coherence in the resulting summary. Nevertheless, sentence extraction summaries can give valuable clues to the main points of a document and are frequently sufficiently intelligible to human readers.

explainer.lead: Sentence extraction is a shallow summarization technique that selects the most salient sentences from a text. It matters because it is a low-cost way to produce summaries without deep linguistic knowledge.

tiers.eli5: It's like highlighting the most important sentences in an article to make a summary, instead of writing new sentences.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use statistical heuristics (e.g., term frequency) to score and select sentences. A pitfall is that extracted summaries often lack coherence because removed sentences create gaps in the narrative.
tiers.paperLevel: Sentence extraction uses statistical heuristics to identify salient sentences as a filter for meaningful content. It is cheaper than knowledge-intensive approaches requiring ontologies or linguistic knowledge, but the major downside is loss of coherence in the resulting summary.

explainer.example: Given a news article, a sentence extractor might pick the first sentence of each paragraph based on word frequency scores, producing a bullet-point style summary.
